questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you slow down other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow).

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while shifting gears:

options.text: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long while shifting, you may have trouble shifting into the next gear. Do not force it. Instead, go back to neutral, release the clutch, speed up the engine to match the road speed, and try again.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, you should not:

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.

questions.explanation: If your engine catches fire, turn off the engine as soon as possible. Do not open the hood if you can help it.

questions.question: You should check your mirrors:

options.text: Only when there may be an emergency.
By having a helper watch your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors on both sides of your vehicle frequently while driving.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer attached. Drivers must be careful when operating one.

questions.question: Which of the following should NOT concern motorists?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
A construction worker on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to the road. Drivers and pedestrians talking may be distracted. Construction workers may not see traffic because they are focused on their work and can distract drivers.

questions.question: Hazardous materials warning signs are usually shaped like:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning signs are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve is used to:

options.text: Check the connection between the trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the "trolley valve" or "Johnson bar") controls the trailer brakes. Use it only for testing. Using it while driving can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: A danger of swerving to avoid an obstacle while driving a large truck is that:

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may stay in the same lane.

questions.explanation: Swerving can sometimes be the safest way to avoid an obstacle. However, it is risky. Top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers can flip over when swerving.

questions.question: If your mirrors are dirty before you start driving:

options.text: They will get clean after driving a short distance.
You do not need to worry about it.

questions.explanation: Before driving, check your mirrors and windshield for dirt. Clean them if needed so you can see clearly.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance your vehicle travels from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brakes
The distance your vehicle travels from when a hazard appears until you see it
The distance your vehicle travels from when you see a hazard until you decide to brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance your vehicle travels from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brakes
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has three parts: perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. Reaction distance is how far your vehicle goes from the moment you think you need to brake to the moment you actually hit the brakes.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only required for vehicles carrying hazardous materials
Only required when driving on interstate highways

questions.explanation: Before each trip, check for emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles (or six fuses or three flares), and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill, a vehicle's speed will likely:
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls a vehicle downhill, causing its speed to increase.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives drivers in that lane time to move out of your way or warn you with their horn. Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, your minimum following distance should be:
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one extra second.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports your vehicle and load while keeping the axles in position. Problems with this system are very dangerous.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Always use turn signals when changing lanes
Only use turn signals if there is a vehicle next to them
Not use a turn signal if the lane change is obvious

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals when changing lanes
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Too much air pressure in a tire:
questions.explanation: Tires should never have too much air pressure. Always check your tire pressure with a gauge during inspections.

questions.question: Vehicles driving behind a truck:

options.text: May not be able to see objects in front of the truck
Usually have a clear view of the road ahead
Do not need to use signals

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be able to see objects in front of the truck
questions.explanation: Your truck blocks the view of drivers behind you. They may not see hazards ahead that make you need to stop. Tap your brakes and warn other drivers before you slow down or stop.
